mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the tightening signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the labor market weakening signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances with declining GDP, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive supply signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the housing sector is a leading indicator of economic activity.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive demand signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 2% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals an inflationary environment with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the inflationary tightening signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.2%, the combined signal indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive labor market signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures by more than 1% in a month signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending is a major driver of economic growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances despite the weakening demand signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
